# Dynamic Array (Arrays and Strings)
Also searched as: dynamic array, resizable array, vector, ArrayList.
Keywords: Dynamic Array, dynamic array, resizable array, vector, ArrayList, Arrays and Strings.

Intuition first: A dynamic array keeps a contiguous buffer with spare capacity so appends are usually free.

## Intuition
A dynamic array keeps a contiguous buffer with spare capacity so appends are usually free.
Before writing any code for Dynamic Array, state this idea back in your own words; if you cannot say what dynamic array is doing, the implementation will only hide the confusion.

## Precise statement
When the buffer is full, capacity is doubled and all n elements are copied; the cost of n appends is O(n), so each append is O(1) amortized.
This is the sentence to reproduce when an examination question asks you to justify Dynamic Array, because it is what separates describing dynamic array from proving that dynamic array is correct.

## Cost
index O(1); append O(1) amortized, O(n) worst case; insert or delete at position i O(n - i).
Report the time and space cost of Dynamic Array separately, and say which case (best, average or worst) each bound refers to.

## How to apply it
Step 1. Spot the signal in the problem statement that points at Dynamic Array: the phrasing usually associated with dynamic array.
Step 2. Write the invariant or recurrence of Dynamic Array on paper and check it on a three-element example before coding.
Step 3. Code the smallest version of Dynamic Array that can be tested, then extend it to the edge cases (empty input, one element, all elements equal).
Step 4. Re-derive the complexity of Dynamic Array from the code you actually wrote.

## Frequent mistake
Students quote O(1) for append as a worst-case bound and forget the occasional O(n) resize.
In the laboratory sessions this single mistake accounts for most of the failing test cases on Dynamic Array, so check for it first when debugging dynamic array.

# Two Pointers (Arrays and Strings)
Also searched as: two pointers, opposite ends, pair sum.
Keywords: Two Pointers, two pointers, opposite ends, pair sum, Arrays and Strings.

Intuition first: Two indices moving toward each other replace a nested loop when the array is sorted.

## Intuition
Two indices moving toward each other replace a nested loop when the array is sorted.
Before writing any code for Two Pointers, state this idea back in your own words; if you cannot say what two pointers is doing, the implementation will only hide the confusion.

## Intuition
Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs so the largest element bubbles to the end.
Before writing any code for Bubble Sort, state this idea back in your own words; if you cannot say what bubble sort is doing, the implementation will only hide the confusion.

## Precise statement
After pass k the last k elements are final; an early exit when no swap occurs makes the best case O(n).
This is the sentence to reproduce when an examination question asks you to justify Bubble Sort, because it is what separates describing bubble sort from proving that bubble sort is correct.

## Cost
time O(n^2) average and worst, O(n) best with the swap flag; space O(1); stable.

Yo concept classroom ma sodhne bela students le "binary search on answer kasari kaam garcha?" bhanera
sodhchan. Tyo bela ma main kura yo ho: Define ok(x) that is false then true; the boundary is found in O(log range) calls to ok.

**Complexity ko kura:** O(log range * cost of ok). Yo line ratne haina, kina yesto huncha bhanera bujhne.
Exam ma "justify your answer" bhaneko cha bhane, maathi ko formal statement lekhnu parcha.

**Sabai bhanda badhi hune galti:** Applying it when the predicate is not monotone, so the boundary is not unique.
